Draft Statement of Work (SOW)
Building 65 Bat Mitigation
 Black Hills VA Health Care System at Fort Meade, South Dakota
General Intention: Contractor shall provide all supervision, tools, labor, materials, hardware, equipment, transportation, and incidentals necessary to complete a turnkey finished project for the following services: 
Professional Bat abatement in attic of Building 65. Remove bat colonies, conduct bat proofing/exclusion, remove bat guano and insulation (sterilize as needed), sanitize the area, and reinstall insulation. Building 65 is a 2-story building with the attic above.
General Requirements:
Contractor shall provide all supervision, labor, materials, equipment, and incidentals necessary to accomplish work elements and requirements outlined in this Statement of Work (SOW).
Where equipment, temporary installations, ingress/egress restrictions or any other consideration is necessary, signage in such areas shall be provided by Contractor.
The Contractor shall confine all staging activities within the anticipated construction area. Contractor shall coordinate proposed staging areas with the facility representative for approval.
The Contractor shall field verify all existing conditions, dimensions, and quantities prior to any work activities. Time and date to be coordinated with facility representative.
Any work that is not addressed by the contract shall immediately be brought to the attention of the Contracting Officer. No  out-of-scope  or additional work shall be executed prior to modification of the contract by the Contracting Officer.
Contractor shall remove all rubbish from the Fort Meade property and dispose off site following VA Specification 01 74 19 Construction Waste Management. Contractor shall record all quantities of materials removed from the Fort Meade property and turn into the facility representative monthly reports even if a null report.
Contractor to perform all work during normal work hours, Monday through Friday 7:00 am to 4:30 pm Mountain Time except as coordinated with the facility representative for any activities that may need to occur outside of normal working hours at no additional cost to the Government.
The requirements of this SOW supplement other related VA standards for construction, space and facility planning criteria, design guides, design manuals, specifications, and details, which remain in full force and effect. Specifically, all requirements of VA handbook 0730, NEC 517, NFPA Health Care Facilities Code for Branches, Security and Law Enforcement, Appendix B, (which covers physical security requirements for VA facilities), the VA fire Protection Design Manual (which covers all VA construction), and ICT standards on the TIL remain in effect.
Work Elements: Which shall include and are not limited to: All supervision, tools, labor, materials, hardware, equipment, transportation, and incidentals necessary to complete a turnkey finished project.
Bat Exclusion:
Bats need to be permanently excluded from roosting in the VA building 65 using non-lethal exclusion methods following Bat Conservation International (BCI), South Dakota Game, Fish and Parks recommendations, and comply with section 7 of the Endangered Species Act. The technique includes using one-way exit devices (industry preferred exclusion tubes VA approved), sealing points of entry, interior and exterior of the building, and preventing access to the building interior. Exclusion activities will be conducted when bats are not present if feasible; this timing will also ensure that activities occur before the Maternity and Roost season. Bat removal shall occur between February 1st, 2027 and April 15th, 2027. Exclusion may not be done when pups are too young to fly (June-August). Change to these timelines may be proposed and accepted after discussion and approval by the designated facility representative(s) and contracting officer.
One-way exit devices through which bats can leave but cannot return are made from tube-type excluders which are placed at all active entry points. Exclusion tubes should have a diameter of two inches, a length of 10 inches with a smooth surface and should project no more than one-quarter inch into the opening.
